points.title: 幼年继位
points.description: 玛丽·斯图亚特于1542年12月8日出生在苏格兰林利思哥宫，是苏格兰国王詹姆斯五世与法国贵族玛丽·德·吉斯的女儿。出生仅六天，她的父亲詹姆斯五世去世，玛丽成为苏格兰女王。由于年幼，她的母亲玛丽·德·吉斯担任摄政。这一时期苏格兰处于英格兰和法国的双重影响下，玛丽作为斯图亚特王朝的继承人，她的出生和继位为苏格兰政治格局带来了新的变数。
points.descriptionEn: Mary Stuart was born on December 8, 1542, at Linlithgow Palace in Scotland, the daughter of King James V and Mary of Guise. Just six days after her birth, her father died, making Mary the Queen of Scotland. As an infant, her mother Mary of Guise served as regent. During this period, Scotland was under the dual influence of England and France. As the heir to the Stuart dynasty, Mary's birth and accession brought new changes to Scotland's political landscape.

points.title: 法国宫廷成长
points.description: 1548年，年仅六岁的玛丽被送往法国，与未来的法国国王弗朗索瓦二世订婚。她在法国宫廷接受了全面的教育，精通多种语言（包括法语、拉丁语、意大利语、西班牙语和英语），学习了文学、音乐、舞蹈、骑术等贵族技能。1558年，她与弗朗索瓦二世结婚，成为法国王后。1560年弗朗索瓦二世去世后，玛丽于1561年8月返回苏格兰，开始亲政。这段法国经历使她深受法国文化影响，也为她日后复杂的政治处境埋下了伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: In 1548, at just six years old, Mary was sent to France to be betrothed to the future French King Francis II. She received a comprehensive education at the French court, mastering multiple languages (including French, Latin, Italian, Spanish, and English), and learning literature, music, dance, horsemanship, and other noble skills. In 1558, she married Francis II and became Queen of France. After Francis II's death in 1560, Mary returned to Scotland in August 1561 to begin her personal reign. This French experience deeply influenced her culture and laid the groundwork for her complex political situation later in life.

points.title: 苏格兰女王统治
points.description: 1561年，玛丽回到苏格兰开始亲政。面对新教改革后的宗教分裂和贵族争权，她试图采取平衡政策，既尊重新教又保留天主教传统。1565年，她与表兄亨利·斯图亚特（达恩利勋爵）结婚，引发政治风波。1566年，她生下未来的詹姆斯六世（后来的英格兰国王詹姆斯一世）。1567年，她的丈夫达恩利勋爵被谋杀，这一事件成为她政治生涯的转折点。同年，她与博斯韦尔伯爵结婚，被怀疑参与谋杀丈夫，导致贵族叛乱。这一系列事件严重损害了她的统治合法性。
points.descriptionEn: In 1561, Mary returned to Scotland to begin her personal reign. Facing religious division after the Protestant Reformation and noble power struggles, she attempted a balanced policy, respecting both Protestantism and Catholic traditions. In 1565, she married her cousin Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley, which caused political turmoil. In 1566, she gave birth to James VI (later James I of England). In 1567, her husband Lord Darnley was murdered, an event that became a turning point in her political career. Later that year, her marriage to the Earl of Bothwell, suspected of involvement in her husband's murder, led to a noble rebellion. This series of events severely damaged the legitimacy of her rule.

points.title: 流亡英格兰
points.description: 1567年，玛丽在贵族叛乱中被废黜，被迫退位，她的儿子詹姆斯六世继位。她逃往英格兰，寻求表姐伊丽莎白一世的庇护。然而，伊丽莎白一世视玛丽为潜在的王位威胁，将她囚禁。玛丽在英格兰度过了近二十年的囚禁生活，先后被关押在多个城堡和庄园。在此期间，她与支持者保持联系，策划多次逃脱和叛乱计划。1586年，巴宾顿阴谋暴露，证明玛丽参与针对伊丽莎白的阴谋，这成为她最终被处决的关键证据。
points.descriptionEn: In 1567, Mary was deposed during a noble rebellion and forced to abdicate, with her son James VI succeeding her. She fled to England, seeking refuge with her cousin Queen Elizabeth I. However, Elizabeth viewed Mary as a potential threat to her throne and imprisoned her. Mary spent nearly twenty years in captivity in England, held in various castles and manors. During this time, she maintained contact with her supporters and planned numerous escape and rebellion plots. In 1586, the Babington Plot was uncovered, proving Mary's involvement in a conspiracy against Elizabeth, which became key evidence for her eventual execution.

points.title: 最终处决
points.description: 1587年2月8日，经过长时间审判和伊丽莎白一世的犹豫，玛丽·斯图亚特在英格兰福瑟黑文城堡被处决。她身着猩红色衣服，象征天主教殉道者，在行刑前保持尊严，拒绝刽子手帮助。她的死引发了欧洲天主教世界的震惊和谴责，也使她成为宗教冲突和权力斗争的象征。玛丽死后，她的儿子詹姆斯六世继承了英格兰王位，结束了两国长期的敌对状态。玛丽的一生充满了戏剧性转折，成为欧洲历史上最具传奇色彩的女性统治者之一。
points.descriptionEn: On February 8, 1587, after a lengthy trial and Elizabeth I's hesitation, Mary Stuart was executed at Fotheringhay Castle in England. Dressed in crimson, symbolizing a Catholic martyr, she maintained her dignity to the end, refusing assistance from the executioner. Her death shocked and condemned Catholic Europe, making her a symbol of religious conflict and power struggles. After Mary's death, her son James VI inherited the English throne, ending the long-standing hostility between the two countries. Mary's life was filled with dramatic turns, making her one of the most legendary female rulers in European history.

supporter.zh: 玛丽·斯图亚特被视为一位悲剧性的女王和天主教信仰的殉道者。支持者认为她是一位优雅、有教养且坚定的统治者，在复杂的宗教和政治环境中努力维护苏格兰的独立和天主教传统。她流亡英格兰期间展现的尊严和勇气，以及面对死亡时的镇定，都体现了她作为王室的尊严。她的支持者认为，她的悲剧命运主要是由于当时宗教冲突和性别偏见所致，而非个人过错。
supporter.en: Mary Stuart is viewed by her supporters as a tragic queen and martyr for the Catholic faith. They see her as an elegant, educated, and steadfast ruler who struggled to maintain Scotland's independence and Catholic traditions amidst complex religious and political circumstances. Her dignity and courage during her exile in England, as well as her composure in the face of death, exemplify royal dignity. Her supporters argue that her tragic fate was primarily due to the religious conflicts and gender biases of her time rather than personal failings.

critic.zh: 批评者认为玛丽·斯图亚特是一位政治判断力不足、感情用事的统治者。他们指责她在处理婚姻关系和权力平衡上的失误，特别是与达恩利勋爵和博斯韦尔伯爵的婚姻，直接导致了她的政治危机。批评者还质疑她参与针对伊丽莎白一世的阴谋，认为她缺乏作为统治者的政治智慧，将个人情感置于国家利益之上。这些批评者认为，她的统治失败主要是由于个人决策失误，而非外部环境的不利。
critic.en: Critics view Mary Stuart as a ruler with poor political judgment and emotional decision-making. They accuse her of mistakes in handling marital relationships and power balances, particularly her marriages to Lord Darnley and the Earl of Bothwell, which directly led to her political crisis. Critics also question her involvement in conspiracies against Elizabeth I, arguing she lacked the political wisdom to prioritize national interests over personal emotions. These critics believe her failed reign was primarily due to personal decision-making errors rather than unfavorable external circumstances.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，玛丽·斯图亚特被定义为一位复杂而矛盾的历史人物。历史学者将她置于16世纪欧洲宗教改革和君主政治变革的背景下，分析她作为女性统治者在男性主导的政治环境中的挑战。她的故事被广泛用于探讨权力、性别、宗教忠诚和个人命运等主题。在流行文化中，她经常被浪漫化为一位悲剧性的美丽女王，成为无数文学、戏剧、电影和歌剧的灵感来源，如《玛丽·斯图亚特》和《伊丽莎白》等作品，展现了她在历史记忆中的持久魅力。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Mary Stuart is defined as a complex and contradictory historical figure. Historians place her within the context of 16th-century European religious reform and monarchical political change, analyzing her challenges as a female ruler in a male-dominated political environment. Her story is widely used to explore themes of power, gender, religious loyalty, and personal destiny. In popular culture, she is often romanticized as a tragic beautiful queen, inspiring countless literary works, plays, films, and operas such as 'Mary Stuart' and 'Elizabeth,' demonstrating her enduring fascination in historical memory.

self.zh: 我生来就是女王，我死后也将是女王。
self.en: I was born a queen, and I shall die a queen.

others.zh: 她拥有所有能够使一个女人成为伟大统治者的品质，除了那些使她能够保持统治的品质。
others.en: She had all the qualities which make a woman a great queen, except those which make a great queen able to keep her throne.
